blocks.text: The chapter describes a high priest as someone appointed by God to represent people before God, offering gifts and sacrifices for sins. This frames Jesus’ priesthood not as self-promotion: he is named a priest “after the order of Melchizedek,” while the chapter also presents him as God’s Son.

Verses 5–10 use words drawn from the Psalms to speak of Jesus’ sonship and priesthood. More broadly, New Testament writers quote and echo psalms when discussing Jesus’ suffering, resurrection, enthronement, priesthood, mission, worship, creation, and the life of believing communities. The extent and significance of particular echoes remains debated.

Papyrus 46 is an early substantial manuscript witness to Hebrews. It contains gaps, and its date is an approximate judgment based on handwriting, so it is valuable evidence without settling every question about the letter’s earliest transmission.
